newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police arrest 20 at student protest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police arrest 20 at student protest.

text.p: Belarus police broke up a protest by about 50 people objecting to President Alexander Lukashenko's policies on Thursday, arresting about 20 of them including an opposition politician.

It was the latest incident of strong-arm tactics by police against peaceful protesters in the former Soviet republic since Lukashenko ordered a clamp-down on rallies and banned nationalist symbols earlier this month.
Seven busloads of police were sent to the protest organised by students to oppose the re-introduction of a Soviet-era scheme under which graduates were appointed to jobs.
Police arrested a member of the former parliament disbanded by Lukashenko last November, Pavel Znavets.
Opposition forces have been promising a "political spring" to the hardline leader who vastly increased his powers after a sweeping victory at a referendum last November.
There was no sign of the red-and-white nationalist symbols and flags which Lukashenko has replaced with Soviet ones.
The protesters opposed Lukashenko's ruling that higher education institutions should appoint students to jobs like in Soviet days -- a decision he said would curb unemployment.
